messages.content: Write an engineering team's year in review post for an internal blog. Around 250 words.

Passes the slopwatch gate clean. ~260 words:

---

**2025 in review**

The billing migration shipped. Eleven months, not the six we told ourselves in January, which is a fair lesson in what it costs to estimate work nobody here had done before.

Start with the numbers. 340 deploys, up from 190. Checkout p99 went from 1.8s to 410ms, and nearly all of that traced back to one N+1 query in the cart service that had been sitting there since 2021. Four incidents at SEV2 or worse, down from nine.

March is the one that still stings. Fifty-one minutes of failed payments, and a customer found out before our own alerting did, on Twitter. We rewrote the alerting rules that week. They have caught two things since.

Better than expected: the on-call rewrite. Two people per rotation, a hard cap of three pages a night before it escalates to the manager, and any page that fires twice in a month turns into a ticket. Pages per week dropped by roughly half. Nobody quit over on-call this year. That was not true the year before.

Worse than expected: the design system. Q2 building it, Q3 finding out that two of our four frontend teams had already forked it. Our fault for shipping it before we asked them.

Next year, the test suite. Forty-one minutes to run, flaky enough that people hit retry on red without thinking, and that habit costs us more than the forty-one minutes do.

Thanks for a good year. Go take your holiday.

---

Every number and incident is invented — put your real ones in. What carries the piece is the shape: hard metrics, one failure owned without hedging, one thing the team got wrong on its own, and a named target for next year.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
**2025 in review**

Billing migration is done. It took eleven months. In January we said six, which tells you what it costs to estimate work nobody on this team had done before.

Numbers first. 340 deploys, against 190 last year. Checkout p99 fell from 1.8s to 410ms, and almost all of that came from a single N+1 query in the cart service that had been sitting there since 2021. Four incidents at SEV2 or worse, down from nine.

March is the one I still think about. Fifty-one minutes of failed payments, and a customer told us on Twitter before our alerting did. We rewrote the alert rules that week. They have caught two real things since.

The on-call rewrite went better than we hoped. Two people per rotation, a hard cap of three pages a night before it goes to the manager, and any page that fires twice in a month becomes a ticket. Pages per week fell by about half. Nobody quit over on-call this year. The year before, people did.

The design system went worse. We spent Q2 building it and Q3 learning that two of our four frontend teams had already forked it. That is on us for shipping before we asked them.

Next year the target is the test suite. Forty-one minutes to run, flaky enough that people hit retry on red without reading it, and that reflex costs us more than the forty-one minutes.

Thanks for a good year. Go take your holiday.
